summary.headline: IndiQube FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,469 crore (+37% YoY) with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 125 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue of INR 1,469 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA above INR 300 crore (+60%) and PAT of INR 125 crore (+145%). Average steady-state occupancy was about 84%, while March 2026 end-of-month occupancy was 81%, which management attributed to newly delivered large properties ramping up. Management guided FY27 to 1.5-2 million sq ft of annual area addition, 25-30% revenue growth, EBITDA margin of 18-21% and PAT margin of 8-10%. Capex per sq ft is rising to about INR 16.5 from INR 15.5, and the company is adding 30-35 MW of solar next year.

financial_highlights.metric: Average revenue per occupied seat per month

financial_highlights.change: Added about 1.6 million sq ft in FY26

segments.name: Flexible workspace (centres)
segments.commentary: Added about 1.6 million sq ft of rent-paying area and launched 15 new centres in FY26; steady-state occupancy 88% per management, versus 87% earlier. Area under management is 9.66 million sq ft, expected to become operational over 18-24 months.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Contributed 15% of revenue in FY26 versus 12% a year earlier; management expects 17-18% over the next year. VAS EBITDA margins are about 10-15%, below the 18-20% space business. Around INR 40 crore of the quarter's VAS was one-time, per an analyst's figure.

segments.name: MiQube platform
segments.commentary: Recorded 1.4 million transactions over the year; new space management module and vehicle pooling feature in transport module gaining traction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 area addition of 1.5-2 million sq ft (33,000-44,000 seats), roughly 1-1.25 lakh sq ft per month of rent-yielding area addition.
FY27 revenue growth of 25-30%, EBITDA margin 18-21%, PAT margin 8-10%.
Lease payments expected to grow in line with revenue.
FY27 capex about INR 1,650 per sq ft of added area, with solar capex of INR 125-150 crore for 30-35 MW of new solar.
VAS contribution expected to rise to 17-18% of revenue.
Rental inflation of 5-10% per year on blended revenue per seat expected (contracts carry 5-6% escalation).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex deployed about INR 414 crore: interiors about INR 250 crore, design-and-build about INR 50 crore, solar about INR 73 crore, vendor payments and advances about INR 30 crore; management said this was above the earlier INR 360 crore guidance mainly due to solar.

Solar: 4 MW plant in Latur, Maharashtra now operational; 20 MW Yadgir, Karnataka operational; 2.7 MW Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu expected operational next quarter. Solar savings estimated at INR 22-23 crore per year.
Plan to add 30-35 MW of solar in FY27 across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra; 40% accelerated depreciation is available on solar.
Capex per sq ft rising to about INR 16.5 from INR 15.5 due to 5-7% material cost increases; not passed to clients.

IPO proceeds of INR 610 crore: INR 462 crore earmarked for capex was reallocated — INR 187 crore to other capital assets (design-and-build interiors INR 55 crore, solar INR 16 crore, security deposits INR 52 crore, real estate/adjacent investments INR 64 crore); general corporate purpose INR 50.4 crore unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did occupancy appear to dip to about 80-81% while area addition was small, and why did capex (about INR 413 crore) exceed the INR 360 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the relevant metric is the FY26 average occupancy of about 84% (a 1% dip), and that quarterly swings are normal. The capex overrun reflected solar investment of about INR 73 crore that generates INR 20-23 crore of annual savings, plus vendor payment timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will lease payments grow in line with revenue next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lease costs will grow in line with revenue, at 25-30%, with EBITDA margin held at 18-21%.

qa_highlights.question: Are IT/ITES tenants reducing footprint, and why do landlords accept 15-year lock-ins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the vertical mix will broadly stay the same with gradual shifts. Landlords accept long lock-ins because the company funds fit-outs, which would be lost on exit, and similar norms exist in hotels and retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for flex and GCCs over the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong absorption, no war impact yet, a weaker rupee boosting India work, and GCC-led absorption; AI impact not yet visible. It sees flex taking 20-25% of large occupiers' portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in one-time VAS revenue, and how will VAS mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time items are upfront sales of IT products, design-and-build and furniture, and are hard to predict; VAS share is expected to rise from 15% to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex per sq ft rising, and what was the IPO fund reallocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material costs rose 5-7% due to the war, taking capex to INR 16.5 per sq ft from INR 15.5, absorbed by the company. The IPO reallocation moved INR 187 crore of capex to design-and-build, security deposits, solar and adjacent investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster given available cash and about 50% headroom in area under management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises sustainable growth and micro-market defensibility, avoids overbuilding, and values landlord relationships; it said it is trying to push growth faster within those limits.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company disclose quarterly rent-paying area additions in advance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed to consider disclosing expected quarterly rent-paying area; it said it adds about 1-1.5 lakh sq ft per month of RPA, with about 1-1.25 lakh sq ft per month of rent-yielding area.

risks_watch: Quarterly occupancy volatility from large deliveries (Q4 end-March occupancy 81% vs 84% annual average); ramp-up takes 9-12 months to reach 90%.
Capex per sq ft rising (INR 15.5 to 16.5), with war-linked material inflation; management is absorbing it.
Dependence on one-time VAS sales, which management cannot predict; VAS margins of 10-15% are below space EBITDA.
Tier-2 expansion still early; management calls it a 10-year story with supply and landlord-maturity issues.
Data-centre and power-intensive client demand requires further solar and power additions.
Commitment to 1.5-2 million sq ft annual additions and 25-30% growth depends on supply pick-up and demand continuity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on growth, margins and guidance, but defensive when pressed on quarterly occupancy dips and the capex overrun. Management repeatedly stressed annual metrics over quarterly ones. It was candid about the Tier-2 story being early and about cautious growth pacing.
key_quotes: We achieved our highest-ever revenue of INR 1,469 crores, representing a growth of 37% year-on-year.
So, quarter-wise fluctuation in a rent-yielding area or area addition should not be viewed in isolation.
Our belief has always been sustainable growth, because we believe that growth at any cost comes at a huge cost.
So, the right way is you look at a year-on-year, 12-month number, because by that time, the property would have stabilized.
demand_pricing: Calendar 2025 gross office absorption about 82.5 million sq ft; Jan-Mar 2026 absorption 20.7 million sq ft; CY26 absorption expected about 5% above CY25, with Bangalore at about 29-30% share. Flex operators took about 23% of absorption and GCCs about 44%.

Management sees no war impact on demand so far, a weaker rupee favouring India work, and no visible AI impact yet. It expects GCC-led absorption over the next couple of years and sees flex taking 20-25% of large occupiers' portfolios.

Pricing: average revenue per occupied seat about INR 192 for FY26. Contracts carry 5-6% escalation; institutional supply priced higher (cited INR 21-30 versus INR 70-80 earlier). Management expects 5-10% annual growth in blended revenue per seat.

Leasing economics: REIT-to-operator rent differential of 5-10% on long tenures and large blocks; 20-25% difference for single floors versus whole buildings in non-institutional supply. Around 90% of uptake is speculative; single-tenant buildings are about 10% of portfolio.

Competition and micro-markets: about 17 cities, with few additions planned; focus on micro-markets above 90% occupancy (e.g., Guindy, OMR, Outer Ring Road, Golf Course Road), avoiding Manesar, North Bangalore and Navi Mumbai with 15-25% vacancy. Institutional share of portfolio rose from 16% to 18%. Tier-2 described as a 10-year story; Coimbatore cited as a promising city. Management described the rental inflation of 4-5% in key micro-markets as sustainable.

adds.what: 1.5-2.0 million sq ft (33,000-44,000 seats) of rent-paying area added in FY27
30-35 MW solar addition across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra in FY27

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 25-30% revenue growth (midpoint 27.5%) is backed by a specific plan to add 1.5-2.0 mn sq ft of rent-paying area, plus 5-10% blended revenue-per-seat growth from contract escalators; partial backing because the 9.66 mn sq ft area under management is only expected to go live over 18-24 months and no quarterly split was given.
